info.title: Fault Management REST APIs
info.description:
The Fault Management application provides a means of investigating faults in a network. A user can view information about faults, such as their causes and impacts. Below is a list of published URLs that can be used in the browser to observe different parts of the application, followed by the API that can be used to obtain information about alarms. Where URL encoding is required (see the individual API requests), this API expects the encoding to use the UTF-8 character-set.

Published URLs

<host>/web/fault-management/current-alarm-list
<host>/web/fault-management/current-alarm-statistics
<host>/web/fault-management/merged-alarm-list
<host>/web/fault-management/historical-alarm-list
<host>/web/fault-management/unhealthy-nes
<host>/web/fault-management/top-problems

<host>/web/fault-management/current-alarm-list?advancedFilter=<alarmId_expression>
Where the value for <alarmId_expression> is an encoded expression: modelFdn="<alarm_id>"

<host>/web/fault-management/current-alarm-list?context1=<context1>
Where the value for <context1> is an encoded object: {"siteId":"<site_id>","siteName":"<site_name>"}

Access Information

Prior to accessing the API services below, the API client must authenticate the NSP user via the NSP REST Gateway's authentication API service. The api-docs for the REST Gateway can be found with the NSP Product at:

https://<server>:<port>/rest-gateway/api-docs/ - where <server> is the hostname/FQDN/IP address of the installed server

or via the NSP DevPortal at:

https://network.developer.nokia.com/api-documentation/ - you will need to create an account on the NSP DevPortal to gain access to the api-docs

To view correlation rules, see Correlation Rule Documentation.

Streaming

When requesting streaming data, use a streaming client to avoid client memory issues or invalid data. Additionally, the "Try it out" button next to the endpoint is not supported for streaming data.
Only one FaultManagement streaming request is allowed at a time.

get.description: Get a paged list of ports, network elements and resource groups that are currently squelched. Default page size is 1000.

requestBody.description: A JSON body containing the FDN of the port, network element or resource group to be squelched. The port or network element FDN can be retrieved from the 'ports' or 'network elements' APIs within the Network Supervision application. Refer to the Network Supervision REST API Documentation. requestBody.description:
JSON compatible string containing parameters and their new values.

The JSON string should contain all of the following parameters.

maxFrequency (int) maximum e-mails per hour, valid range 1 - 10

requestBody.description:
JSON compatible string containing parameters and their new values.

The JSON string should contain at least one of the following parameters.

autoAck (boolean) - Automatically acknowledge incoming alarms.

autoDeletionDays (int) - Delete after (days); min=1 max=30

deEscalationPolicy - De-Escalation Threshold (severity, type, value)

debouncingEnabled (boolean) - Enable or disable alarm debouncing. Only applies to implicitly cleared alarms.

debouncingHoldPeriod (int) - The amount of time in seconds for which an alarm should be held when debounced; min=10 max=600

escalationPolicy - Escalation Threshold (severity, type, value)

historyEnabled (boolean) - Log alarm history.

initialSeverity (string) - Override incoming alarm severity.

squelch (boolean) - Drop and do not record incoming alarms.

useAlarmPolicyAging(boolean) - Enable or disable aging at policy level. Cannot be enabled if useGlobalAging is enabled. Only applies to non implicitly cleared alarms.

useGlobalAging (boolean) - Use the defined global aging settings. Cannot be enabled if useAlarmPolicyAging is enabled. Only applies to non implicitly cleared alarms.

userText (string) - Add up to 4096 characters of custom text.

parameters.description: The FDN of the port, network element or resource group to be unsquelched. (Double URL encoded)

additionalText.description:
A free form text description to be reported by the source.
Alarms can be customized using this field.
The value in the newly created alarm will be prepended with "FOR LAB USE ONLY".
The maximum number of characters allowed is 4096, including the prefix "FOR LAB USE ONLY - ".

affectedObject.description:
The source identifier of the object that the alarm is affecting.
Must be in a valid modelFdn format i.e. "fdn:<scheme>:<namespace>:<fdn>".
All alarms sharing the same affectedObject value also share the same UAC applicability rules. For that reason:
  • All alarms raised with a given affectedObject must share the same affectedObjectType
  • When an alarm is raised for a given affectedObject with a neId corresponding to a NetworkElement, any other alarm raised with the same affectedObject must be raised with the same neId

Examples: For WS-NOC alarms, this is the FDN of the affected object on the NFM.
That value is used to cross launch to the NFM.
Alarm on a Network Element -> The FDN of the network element as known by its data source (MDM adaptors)
Alarm on any equipment children of an NE; shelf, card, port, etc. -> The FDN of the equipment as known by its data source (i.e. MDM adaptors)
Alarm on a service -> The FDN of the service as known by its data source (e.g. SF)
Alarm on a service site -> The FDN of the service site as known by its data source (e.g. SF)

affectedObjectName.description: The displayed name of the affected object.

affectedObjectType.description:
The type of the affected object.
The restrictions below are required for FM features such as access control and alarm squelching:
  • When the affected object is persisted in NSP, the value must correspond to the NSP entity type for which that affected object is persisted i.e. "<model.name>.<entity.name>"
  • When the affected object is not persisted in NSP, then the value must not be equal to any existing NSP entity types

alarmName.description:
The name of the alarm.
The value should use CamelCase notation with a leading capital.
Avoid ending the value with the word "Alarm" which is redundant.
Consider reusing existing alarm names where applicable.

alarmType.description:
The broad category of the alarm.
The value should use camelCase notation with a leading lowercase.
The complete list of expected values below corresponds to ITU-T X.733 or other standards, such as ITU-T M.3100, 2G and 3G.
  • communicationsAlarm: Principally associated with the procedures and/or processes required to convey information from one point to another
  • environmentalAlarm: Principally associated with a condition relating to an enclosure in which the equipment resides
  • equipmentAlarm: Principally associated with an equipment fault
  • integrityViolationAlarm: An indication that information may have been illegally modified, inserted or deleted
  • operationalViolationAlarm: An indication that the provision of the requested service was not possible due to the unavailability, malfunction or incorrect invocation of the service
  • physicalViolationAlarm: An indication that a physical resource has been violated in a way that suggests a security attack
  • processingErrorAlarm: Principally associated with a software or processing fault
  • qualityOfServiceAlarm: Principally associated with a degradation in the quality of a service
  • securityServiceOrMechanismViolationAlarm: An indication that a security attack has been detected by a security service or mechanism
  • timeDomainViolationAlarm: An indication that an event has occurred at an unexpected or prohibited time.
  • unknownAlarm
enum: communicationsAlarm, environmentalAlarm, equipmentAlarm, integrityViolationAlarm, operationalViolationAlarm, physicalViolationAlarm, processingErrorAlarm, qualityOfServiceAlarm, securityServiceOrMechanismViolationAlarm, timeDomainViolationAlarm, unknownAlarm

firstTimeDetected.description:
The first time the alarm condition was detected, in UNIX Epoch time.
The Network Element usually provides this value.

impact.description:
WS-NOC specific.
The impact count of the alarm.
The impact count represents the total number of other alarms caused by this alarm.
When provided and greater than 0, the impact value is not calculated by the Fault Management application.

implicitlyCleared.description: Indicates if an alarm will be automatically cleared by the source after the raising condition is resolved.

lastTimeDetected.description:
The most recent time the alarm condition was detected, in UNIX Epoch time.
The Network Element usually provides this value.

neId.description:
This field is required if the alarm is raised on an Network Element or any entity which is associated with a specific NE.
This allows the Fault Management application to associate the alarm to an NE.
In this case, the neId is the IP of the NE.
For system wide alarms, this field does not need to be specified.
Examples: 11.22.33.44 (ipv4), 2001:0DB8:85A3:0:0:8A2E:370:7334 (ipv6)

neName.description:
If the alarm is raised on an NE or any entity which is associated with a specific NE,
the neName corresponds to the name of the NE.
If not provided, the Fault Management application will try to get the neName from the equipment model.
For system wide alarms, this field does not need to be specified.

nodeTimeOffset.description:
The time offset of the NMS or Network Element where the alarm occurred.
Used internally for WS-NOC alarms to calculate firstTimeDetectedNms,
and for LTE alarms to calculate lastTimeDetectedNode and firstTimeDetectedNode.

numberOfOccurrences.description:
The number of times the alarm has been raised.
Deleting the alarm should reset the count.
When provided and greater than 0, the number of occurrences value is not calculated by the Fault Management application.

objectFullName.description: The fdn of the alarm; "<sourceSystem>:<objectFullName>" form the full source of the alarm.

probableCause.description:
The most likely cause of the alarm.
The value should use camelCase notation with a leading lowercase.
The complete list of expected values below corresponds to ITU-T X.733 or other standards, such as ITU-T M.3100, 2G and 3G.
Refer to ITU-T X.733 for explanation of the ITU-T X.733 values.

rootCause.description:
WS-NOC specific.
Whether the alarm is a root cause or not.
An alarm is a root cause if it was not caused by another alarm.
When provided, the root cause value is not calculated by the Fault Management application.

severity.description:
The severity of the alarm. Refer to ITU-T X.733 for a full description of possible severities.
  • Indeterminate: Indicates that the severity level cannot be determined.
  • Warning: Indicates the detection of a potential or impending service affecting fault, before any significant effects have been observed. Action should be taken to further diagnose (if necessary) and correct the problem in order to prevent it from becoming service affecting fault.
  • Minor: Indicates the existence of a non-service affecting fault condition and that corrective action should be taken in order to prevent a more serious fault becoming service affecting fault.
  • Major: Indicates that a service affecting condition has developed and an urgent corrective action is required.
  • Critical: Indicates that a service affecting condition has occurred and an immediate corrective action is required.
enum: critical, major, minor, warning, condition, info, indeterminate
